messages:
Alex H: Heads up — saw ~40% more spot evictions in us-west1 this morning when a big batch job landed. Affected training queues, some retries spiked.
capacity-bot: [signal] us-west1 G4 preemptible supply down 35% vs baseline, ETA recovery ~2h.
Priya S: Was that from a price spike or capacity reallocation? We were on price-optimized bids for those pools.
Marco L: Price chasing tends to put us in the most volatile AZs. Suggest switching those pools to a capacity-weighted bid and adding a small warm buffer (10% of pool size) to absorb churn.
Samir: Agreed. Also diversify instance families across pools (p3/p4/p4d) and prefer cross-region pools for non-latency-sensitive workloads.
Jin K: Draft policy I was experimenting with — minimal fields, surge factor + weights:
```json
{
  "policy": "weighted_capacity",
  "region_weights": {"us-west1": 0.6, "us-central1": 0.4},
  "instance_family_weights": {"p4": 0.7, "p3": 0.3},
  "surge_factor": 1.15,
  "warmbuffer_pct": 0.10,
  "fallback": ["regional-on-demand", "smaller-instance-spot"]
}
```
Priya S: Nice. What's the rollout plan and minimal acceptance criteria?
Alex H: Canary on batch pools first (non-prod), enable for one cluster, monitor eviction-rate, time-to-fill, and tail queue latency for 2h. Goal: drop eviction rate to <5% and keep cost delta <8% vs previous baseline.
Marco L: Add soft-eviction TTL (drain-in-place) of 60s so long-running jobs can checkpoint, and autoscaler warmups (scale-up buffer) for surge windows.
capacity-bot: [action] Applying weighted_capacity policy to batch-pool-2 at 11:00 UTC.
Samir: I'll wire an alert: if eviction_rate > 10% for 15m => roll back policy and move jobs to price-optimized fallback. Also create metric: cost_per_vgpu_hour and expected savings projection.
Priya S: Please update runbook with the new metrics (evictions/min, time-to-fill, cost_per_vgpu_hour) and a checklist for rollback. Include the small config snippet.
Alex H: Will open a PR with the policy + Grafana dashboard links and a canary playbook. Action list: PR (Alex), alerts (Samir), runbook update (Priya), monitor canary (Marco). :thumbsup:
Priya S: :eyes: I'll review the PR after it's up.
Alex H: Thanks — let's aim to start the canary in the next maintenance window.
